detail:
The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) describes osteoporosis as a disease in which bones lose mass and structural tissue deteriorates, making bones weaker and more likely to break. Bone is living tissue that is constantly broken down and rebuilt, and osteoporosis develops when bone loss outpaces new bone formation. NIAMS notes that the disease often progresses without symptoms until a fracture occurs, which is why it is sometimes called a silent disease.

NIAMS notes that when symptoms do appear, they can include back pain caused by a fractured or collapsed vertebra, loss of height over time, a stooped posture, and fractures that occur more easily than expected, commonly at the hip, spine, and wrist. Risk factors described in sources include advancing age, being female, family history, low body weight, certain medical conditions, and long-term use of certain medicine classes. Clinicians usually diagnose osteoporosis with a bone mineral density test, most commonly a DXA scan, together with medical history and fracture risk assessment.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about osteoporosis symptoms and bone density testing.

title: Osteoporosis: when bones lose strength silently
